saints.name: Pope St. Martin I
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The last pope to die a martyr, exiled and starved for condemning heresy about Christ's will…
biography: Born near Todi in Umbria, Martin had served Pope Theodore I as apocrisiarius, his legate at the imperial court of Constantinople, when he was himself elected; he was consecrated on 21 July 649 without waiting for the emperor's confirmation — a deliberate defiance. Within three months he summoned the bishops of the West to the Lateran.

That council, 105 bishops in October 649, condemned Monothelitism — the doctrine that Christ had but one will — together with the Ecthesis of Heraclius and the Typos by which Constans II forbade the whole dispute. Constans struck back: in June 653 the exarch Theodore Calliopas seized the ailing pope in the Lateran basilica and shipped him prisoner to Constantinople.

Tried there for treason, publicly degraded, and condemned to death, he saw his sentence commuted to exile; in May 655 he reached Cherson in the Crimea, where famine and neglect killed him within months, on 16 September 655. The Church venerates him as the last of the martyr popes, and the East keeps him as Saint Martin the Confessor.
saints.knownFor: Condemning Monothelitism and dying in exile for the faith.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 April
